rationale: Shed Cam shows RSSI -87 dBm (below the -80 dBm threshold for reliable operation), intermittent status with 9 heartbeat losses in 24h, and choppy/freezing live view — all classic weak-signal symptoms. The customer confirmed the camera streams perfectly when moved closer to the base station, and the new metal garden fence (installed last month) is the attenuating obstruction. This is an L1 signal issue, not a hardware fault; a replacement unit would not resolve it.

repair_steps: Confirm with customer that Shed Cam works reliably when moved closer to base station (e.g., at back door).
Instruct customer to permanently relocate Shed Cam to a position with better signal, or move base station to reduce obstruction from metal fence.
If relocation is not possible, recommend installing the official RP-1 repeater between shed and house.
After adjustment, verify RSSI in Device Settings > Device Info is above -80 dBm (ideally above -70 dBm).
Monitor Shed Cam for 24 hours to ensure no further heartbeat losses or intermittent status.

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
